summary.headline: Medanta FY26 total income rose 20% to INR 45,089 million and Q4 set a record, with Noida losses narrowing to INR 236 million in Q4.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with total income up 25% YoY to INR 11,958 million and PAT up 40% YoY to INR 1,417 million. Full-year PAT rose 15.1% to INR 5,541 million, while EBITDA including Noida was INR 10,560 million (24.2% margin). The newly inaugurated 550-bed Noida hospital ramped up, with its quarterly EBITDA loss narrowing from INR 320 million in Q3 to INR 236 million in Q4. Management guided to Noida breakeven in 2H FY27 and laid out a capex and bed-addition pipeline of roughly 2,700 beds over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Mature hospitals (Gurugram, Indore, Ranchi)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 28,482 million (+9%) and EBITDA INR 6,946 million (+7%), margin 24.4% (down ~40 bps). Q4 revenue INR 7,257 million (+11%), EBITDA INR 1,935 million (+15%), margin 26.7%.

segments.name: Developing hospitals excluding Noida
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 14,130 million (+29%) and EBITDA INR 4,470 million (+35%), margin 31.5% vs 30.1%. Q4 revenue INR 3,728 million (+33%), EBITDA INR 1,207 million (+42%), margin 32.4%.

segments.name: Noida (new 550-bed hospital)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 906 million and EBITDA loss INR 783 million; Q3 peak loss INR 320 million, Q4 revenue INR 525 million with loss INR 236 million. Operational 382 beds, 98 ICU beds, 14 OTs; occupancy around 30% currently.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 international patient revenue INR 679 million (+22% YoY); FY26 revenue INR 2,780 million (+33%). Middle East and Bangladesh weak; Africa, Southeast Asia and CIS growing.

segments.name: OPD Pharmacy
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 496 million, up 46.2% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Noida expected to break even in 2H FY27; management declined a firm Q2 FY27 breakeven commitment, citing accumulated losses and a 40-45% occupancy threshold.
Mature hospital EBITDA margin expected to stay in the 24-25% range; no margin guidance formally given.
Capex of about INR 800-900 crore in FY27 and INR 600-700 crore in FY28; total 5-year pipeline capex about INR 45,000 million.
Short term: about 500 beds to be added in existing hospitals at minimal capex; about 2,700 beds via 5 greenfield projects over 3-4 years (Guwahati, Varanasi, South Delhi, Mumbai, Pitampura).
Patna and Lucknow to add beds and about 4-5 OTs each in 1H FY27; Gurugram to add about 5-10 procedural rooms next year.
capex_capacity: FY26 bed capacity rose 20.5% with 623 beds added: 382 at Noida, 131 at Patna, and a 110-bed Ranchi hospital.
Varanasi 400-bed project approved in March 2026 under build-to-suit lease; Medanta's capex limited to MEP, interiors and medical equipment.
Guwahati 400+ bed land acquired; regulatory approvals secured. South Delhi site 1 diaphragm wall complete, civil tender expected by end of next month.
Indore 80-bed hospital acquired via business transfer agreement (May 2026), expected operational in Q2 FY27 to add oncology.
Greenfield hospitals take about 3 years from construction start to finish; management sees May 2029 as the earliest, likely FY30 rather than FY29.
demand_pricing: ARPOB FY26 INR 66,550 (+6.1%); Q4 INR 66,687 (+5%). Mature Q4 ARPOB INR 74,941 (+7%); developing ARPOB FY26 INR 56,500 (+4%).
Occupancy about 62% FY26 on expanded capacity (64% ex-Noida); Q4 about 61% (64% ex-Noida). ALOS fell to 3.04 days in FY26 from 3.17 days.
Inpatient count +16% and outpatient count +19% in FY26; Q4 IPD +23%, OPD +27%.
Noida ARPOB currently around INR 70,000-80,000 but on a 100% cash base and small sample; management expects it to converge with Gurugram.
Patna and Lucknow occupancy around 68% in Q4 (Patna near 70%); Patna has had no tariff increase in about 4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can Noida reach breakeven by Q2 FY27 and what was its occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects breakeven in 2H FY27, not a firm Q2 commitment. Current occupancy is around 30%; breakeven typically needs 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Noida's ramp-up structurally different from Lucknow and Patna?
qa_highlights.answer: Structurally no; the difference is that Lucknow and Patna opened during COVID. Noida is still missing pediatrics (started late FY27), obstetrics, and liver transplant.

qa_highlights.question: Gurugram demand and retention with new competitor hospitals coming in Sept-Oct?
qa_highlights.answer: No senior clinician lost so far. Management expects a war for talent and manpower cost pressure but is not worried on demand.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 and FY28 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR 800-900 crore; FY28 about INR 600-700 crore. Project-wise split not shared.

qa_highlights.question: Growth levers over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Adding services and specialties, bed additions across existing hospitals, about 10 OTs in existing hospitals, and minimally invasive and robotic work.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic plans given strong net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Several acquisition, partnership and O&M transactions under evaluation; no further deals disclosed beyond Indore.

risks_watch: Noida breakeven timing and occupancy ramp (currently about 30%) versus the 40-45% breakeven threshold.
Competitive supply in Gurugram from new hospitals expected around Sept-Oct, with possible clinician attrition and higher manpower costs.
Middle East and Bangladesh disruption to international revenue.
Mature-hospital margin pressure from employee costs; Gurugram carries all corporate costs.
Execution of the 2,700-bed greenfield pipeline and Varanasi, Guwahati and South Delhi timelines; FY30 slippage flagged by management.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 results and growth outlook, while candid that Noida breakeven timing depends on occupancy and that Gurugram's competitive intake and manpower costs need watching. Management was evasive on firm timing commitments (Noida breakeven, greenfield dates) and declined project-level capex detail.
key_quotes: So we do expect this unit to break-even during the course of this year.
We have not taken a single rupee of tariff increase in Patna.
Maybe if you are sitting in May of 2026, you could say May of 2029 hospitals could be up and running. But that may not be FY29 numbers, that may be more FY30 numbers.
We are feeling fairly confident about the margin profile remaining in this kind of 24% - 25% range.
